failure_classification.evidence: All five rejected keyword examples were date-bearing SEC filing queries; the old rule treated ISO dates as internal identifiers.
failure_classification.change: Reject UUID and explicit pipeline/source/fact IDs, while preserving legitimate dates.

failure_classification.evidence: The entity recognizer formed `Q Apple Inc` from the `10-Q` filing label; two Japanese outputs rendered source-backed USD as United States Dollar, which the proper-name-only rule miscategorized.
failure_classification.change: Treat the post-hyphen Q as a form label and accept the United States Dollar alias only when the cited source explicitly contains USD/U.S. dollars.

failure_classification.evidence: The Fed English output repeats a 28-word source run: `the Federal Reserve Board on Tuesday released the minutes from its recent meetings to review and determine the discount rates provided to depository institutions through the discount window`.
The SEC Korean draft title/keyword remains `Apple Inc. 10-Q filed 2026-07-31`; its core phrase is English despite a Korean title prefix and Korean body.

content_volume_assessment.interpretation: These are short source-grounded briefs (one Fed source with five facts; one SEC filing with four facts), not evidence of full-length blog quality. Semantic accuracy, naturalness, rights, and reader value still need human review.
content_volume_assessment.generation_token_measurement: The one SEC-ko Phase 4-L inference artifact reports 256 completion tokens across five calls (outline plus four fact-localization calls); this is aggregate pipeline output, not a body-only token count.
